title: Sandbox evidence review
description: Structured record of a reader's screenshot-by-screenshot review of a Sandbox validation round's evidence. Written by the round to evidence/evidence-review.v1.json (next to evidence/retrospective.md) and asserted at finalize by scripts/sandbox/check_coverage.py's check_evidence_review(). Exists because check_coverage's own filename-token match (check_surface/check_shape) proves a screenshot's NAME claims a surface -- it structurally cannot prove the PIXELS show it. A measured probe planted a mislabeled-but-real capture (right bytes, wrong claim) into a copy of a real round's evidence: the filename-token gate credited it 0/4, three independent blind readers caught it 4/4, 4/4, 4/4. Only a reader closes that gap, so this file makes the reader step a required, mechanically fail-closed tier instead of an optional judgment call. Authoring procedure: scripts/sandbox/sandbox-CLAUDE.md 'Writing results' -> 'Evidence review'. This schema is documentation/reference; check_coverage.py validates the loaded JSON directly (pure stdlib, no jsonschema dependency) rather than validating against this file at runtime -- keep the two in sync by hand when either changes.

version.description: Schema version. Bump (and rename the file, evidence-review.v2.json, etc.) on a breaking shape change.

examined.description: Every credit-eligible screenshot (an image file in the evidence dir at or above check_coverage.py's MIN_SCREENSHOT_BYTES floor) the reader actually opened and looked at, by filename exactly as it appears in the evidence dir (matched case-insensitively at check time). This is the load-bearing coverage assertion's enumerable list: check_evidence_review() fails closed if any credit-eligible screenshot present in the evidence dir is absent from this list. A reader that exhausts its budget mid-set must leave the un-opened files OUT of `examined` and report a partial review -- padding this list with unopened files converts a legible, fail-closed 'incomplete review' into an indistinguishable-from-clean pass, which is the exact silent-gap this file exists to close.

mismatches.description: Screenshots whose FILENAME (or its place in coverage-manifest.json) makes a claim the PIXELS do not support. A filename is a claim; the pixels are the evidence -- an honestly-named blank/wrong capture still belongs here, because an honest name for a non-evidencing capture is still not evidence. Any non-empty `mismatches` list is BLOCKING: check_evidence_review() fails the round closed regardless of how the rest of coverage reads. A review that finds a lie and lets the round pass anyway is decoration, not a review.

file.description: Filename exactly as it appears in the evidence dir.

claims.description: What the filename (or its manifest entry) asserts this capture proves, e.g. the surface/shape token or journey step it is supposed to document.

shows.description: What the pixels actually depict, in the reader's own words -- the contradiction that makes this a mismatch.

uncertain.description: Screenshots the reader could not confidently confirm OR refute against their filename's claim (partial occlusion, an ambiguous crop, a state that could plausibly be either the claimed surface or a neighbouring one). Non-blocking -- reported for human follow-up, not fail-closed -- because an unresolved doubt is a different class of defect than a confirmed mismatch; folding it into `mismatches` would pressure a reader to either suppress real doubt (silently promote it to a false clean pass) or over-claim certainty it doesn't have (a false mismatch) just to avoid ambiguity.

reason.description: Why the reader could not resolve this one either way.

mismatches.shows: the command palette overlay, not the logs surface

uncertain.reason: a toast partially covers the panel underneath; can't confirm the empty-state copy is fully visible
